**A1. System overview**

The Volunteer ID Badge System (VIB) is a colour-coded identification system used across all Northstead CHOP sites. Badges are issued to volunteers, staff, and regular contractors. The system was introduced in March 2023 to replace the old paper visitor book at Marlowe Walk and St. Jude's Church Hall. The Riverside Mobile Unit was added to the scheme in June 2023.

Badge colours indicate the holder's status and access level. The colour scheme is defined in the Badge system manual, S03, which is kept in the IT office and available on the shared drive (folder: Policies/Volunteer_ID_Badge_System). A summary of the colour meanings is reproduced below for reference.

**Badge colour meanings (current controlled entry, verified against manual S03):**

- **Blue** – Active volunteer, standard access (all public areas, volunteer room, kitchen)
- **Green** – Active staff member, full access (including offices and store rooms)
- **Yellow** – Temporary/contractor access (issued for a maximum of 14 days)
- **Orange** – Trainee or probationary volunteer (issued for first 6 weeks)
- **Red** – Expired badge (no longer valid; must be returned to IT office or collection point)
- **Grey** – Retired/superseded badge (no longer in circulation; kept for audit purposes)

The badge system manual states that in Volunteer ID Badge System, the colour of expired badges is red. Record status: historical. This is a historical entry in the manual and remains the current controlled entry as of the last review on 2024-09-30. No change to the colour scheme has been proposed.

**A1. System overview**

The Volunteer ID Badge System (VIB) is a colour-coded identification system used across all Northstead CHOP sites. Badges are issued to volunteers, staff, and regular contractors. The system was introduced in March 2023 to replace the old paper visitor book at Marlowe Walk and St. Jude's Church Hall. The Riverside Mobile Unit was added to the scheme in June 2023.

Badge colours indicate the holder's status and access level. The colour scheme is defined in the Badge system manual, S03, which is kept in the IT office and available on the shared drive (folder: Policies/Volunteer_ID_Badge_System). A summary of the colour meanings is reproduced below for reference.

**Badge colour meanings (current controlled entry, verified against manual S03):**

- **Blue** – Active volunteer, standard access (all public areas, volunteer room, kitchen)
- **Green** – Active staff member, full access (including offices and store rooms)
- **Yellow** – Temporary/contractor access (issued for a maximum of 14 days)
- **Orange** – Trainee or probationary volunteer (issued for first 6 weeks)
- **Red** – Expired badge (no longer valid; must be returned to IT office or collection point)
- **Grey** – Retired/superseded badge (no longer in circulation; kept for audit purposes)

The badge system manual states that in Volunteer ID Badge System, the colour of expired badges is red. Record status: historical. This is a historical entry in the manual and remains the current controlled entry as of the last review on 2024-09-30. No change to the colour scheme has been proposed.

**MEMO — Scheduling and Meeting Records**
**Northstead Community Health Outreach Programme**
**October–December 2024 (with Summer Campaign extension notes)**

**To:** All staff and volunteers
**From:** Marcus Webb, Programme Coordinator
**Date:** 30 September 2024
**Re:** October timetable, Winter Review update, and Summer Campaign extension

---

**1. October timetable**

Please find below the October schedule. A few notes before the table:

- The **HCV testing drop-in** continues on alternate Wednesdays. In October, the drop-in will run on 9 and 23 October only. On the off weeks (2, 16, 30 October), CH, Room 2 is available for other bookings — please check with me before confirming external groups, as we are holding two of those slots for the Summer Campaign extension work.
- **Volunteer Training Level 1** — the October course is now open for booking. J. Okafor is taking names. The course runs over three Wednesdays (16, 23, 30 October) in WC. Please note the 16 October session will start at **14:30** rather than 14:00, as the room is being used for a Summer Campaign planning session in the morning.
- **Room booking note:** the **Knitting circle** has asked to move from WC to GH from 15 October. This is confirmed for the rest of the year. Please update any printed copies of the room booking sheet.
- **Summer Campaign extension** — as you will have seen in the earlier memo, the outreach campaign has been extended to the end of November. This means some of our regular bookings are affected in October and November. The main changes are:
  - The **Blood Pressure clinic (external)** will not run on Mondays in October. They have been offered Tuesday mornings instead. Please see the table for the new slots.
  - The **Benefits advice session** moves from Thursdays to Fridays for October and November. This is to free up LC for the campaign's admin work. The session will run 10:00–12:00 in LC on Fridays, starting 4 October.
  - We have added a **weekly campaign coordination call** on Wednesday afternoons (15:30–16:15) in CH, Room 1. This is for staff only. Volunteers do not need to attend, but if you are helping with the campaign, please speak to A. Patel or me if you have questions that need raising.

**2. Winter Review 2024 — date confirmation**

The Autumn Review 2024 (now being referred to as the **Winter Review 2024**, as the sessions have slipped) is still in the planning stage. The draft schedule indicated the publication date of **12 December 2024**; this remains tentative. I will confirm once the review timetable is finalised. The review sessions themselves will take place in the first two weeks of November — more on this in a separate memo.
